learning: Pending race. Check whether line_loss_events fall toward 0 and whether max_error drops below 0.06 m. If the robot stays on track but does not complete, the next lever is speed.
notes: Adds the Builder's seven-sensor, 16 mm, y = 0.03 m array with proportional weights (about 33 × x) and keeps the iteration 0 gains and speed, so the race isolates the sensing change. Evidence: iteration 0 ended all 60 trials off track at about 0.062 m with about one line-loss event each.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced 60 trials with zero completions. All runs ended off track at about 0.062 m max error, with about one line-loss event each. The robot loses the line at about the same lateral offset where it leaves the track, so the controller needs a sensing array that keeps the tape visible further out. The Builder's proposal widens the array to seven sensors at x = ±0.06 m, uses 16 mm footprints and places the row at y = 0.03 m. I kept the controller's gains, speed and line-loss rule unchanged (kp 3.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.4, last_direction), so that any change in result comes from sensing. Sensor weights are set proportional to lateral position, about 33.3 × x, which gives ±2 at the outer sensors, inside the ±2 limit. This keeps the signal scale close to iteration 0 at the same offsets, while the outer sensors now reach a larger offset before saturating. The main risk is that the weights may overreact when the outer sensors read partial tape at 16 mm. If the next race shows the robot staying on track but not completing, the next test should be speed rather than gain. Expected result is fewer line-loss events and max_error under 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend. This is an estimate, not a measured result.
